cpu.desc: CPU allocation in threads. 100% = 1 thread, 200% = 2 threads, 1000% = 10 threads

disk.desc: Disk space allocation in MB (10240 MB = 10 GB)

memory.desc: How much memory in MB to allocate. 1024 MB runs simple workflows, give more for big data or many executions

ip.desc: What IP to bind the server to

port.desc: Port of the n8n editor and webhooks (TCP, HTTP)

version.desc: Tag of the n8nio/n8n image: stable (newest release), beta, or an exact version such as 2.46.6. Reinstall to download the newest image of the tag. Going back to an older version is not supported

publicurl.desc: Address people and webhooks use to reach n8n, for example https://n8n.example.com/ (behind a reverse proxy) or http://203.0.113.10:5678/. Empty shows localhost in webhook URLs

httpsproxy.desc: Turn on when n8n is reached through an HTTPS reverse proxy (Nginx, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel). It sends the login cookie over HTTPS only and trusts the proxy's X-Forwarded-For. Leave off to log in over plain http://

timezone.desc: Timezone of Schedule Trigger and date nodes, as a TZ database name such as Europe/Madrid, America/Mexico_City or UTC

encryptionkey.desc: Key that encrypts the saved credentials. Empty means n8n creates one on first start and keeps it in .n8n/config. Set it only to move an existing n8n here, with the key it already used

dbtype.desc: Where n8n keeps workflows, credentials and executions. SQLite is a file in the server folder; PostgreSQL is better for many executions

dbhost.desc: Only for PostgreSQL. Address of the database server, for example the node address of a PostgreSQL server created in this panel

dbport.desc: Only for PostgreSQL. Port of the database server

dbname.desc: Only for PostgreSQL. Database n8n uses; it must exist

run.command: sh -c "set -e; [ -n \"$WEBHOOK_URL\" ] || unset WEBHOOK_URL; [ -n \"$N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL\" ] || unset N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL; [ -n \"$N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY\" ] || unset N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY; if [ \"$N8N_SECURE_COOKIE\" = true ]; then export N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1; fi; exec tini -- /docker-entrypoint.sh start"
